summary: A humorous local-interest piece about fishing in a riverside town, promoting the annual "Reel Big Fish" contest at Willow Bend Lake on September 7th, 2023. It tours local fishing spots, introduces angling clubs, and shares comic anecdotes from members about the one that got away, rookie blunders and failed lures. It closes by stressing that the joy of fishing is the real catch.
one_line: A lighthearted guide to the town's fishing hotspots, clubs and funny angler stories, centered on the September 7th, 2023 "Reel Big Fish" contest.
key_facts: The annual "Reel Big Fish" contest is set for September 7th, 2023, at Willow Bend Lake.
Willow Bend Lake is described as an anglers' paradise teeming with largemouth bass.
Whisker Creek is a popular haunt for catfish anglers and home to a legendary catfish named Whiskers who has outwitted many fishers.
Rippleton River has fast-running water and is favored by local fly-fishing virtuosos.
The "Nimble Reelers" club was founded by Bob "The Bass Whisperer" Jenkins on September 19th, 2023, and is known for a light-hearted approach to fishing.
"Gone Fishin' Gals" is a women's angling group led by Sally 'Spinner' McPhee.
Jim "The Jig" Thompson hooked a huge fish on the chilly morning of October 11th, 2023, but the line snapped after a marathon tussle.
Jenny "Tanglefoot" Davis cast her line into foliage instead of water as a beginner because she ignored wind direction, and has since become a champion.
Sam "Snaggletooth" Rodriguez believes fish can sense a newbie; on his first outing he brought a tackle box full of gadgets and caught nothing.
Eric "Easy Cast" Donaldson made a homemade lure from old bottle caps and sequins that caught more jokes than fish and sank to the bottom.
The article ends with the message that "the true catch is the joy we reel in, which is always in season."
